Sends a ray from one point to another through the bodies of a physics world and returns the closest body it hits. All points are in the world. The ray sees bodies where their entities are now, including a body that the program moved since the last `PhysicsUpdate`. It does not see legacy colliders or the meshes of `LinePick`, which are a different world.

What was hit is kept for `GetPhysicsHitEntity`, `GetPhysicsHitX`, `GetPhysicsHitY`, `GetPhysicsHitZ`, `GetPhysicsHitNX`, `GetPhysicsHitNY`, `GetPhysicsHitNZ` and `GetPhysicsHitDistance` until the next ray or point query.

```blitzbasic
body = PhysicsRayCast(0, 10, 0, 0, -10, 0)
If body
	Print "Hit at height " + GetPhysicsHitY()
EndIf
```
@param x1 Where the ray starts, x.
@param y1 Where the ray starts, y.
@param z1 Where the ray starts, z.
@param x2 Where the ray ends, x. Bodies behind this point are not hit.
@param y2 Where the ray ends, y.
@param z2 Where the ray ends, z.
@param mask_low The layers to look at, as bits 0 to 31 of a mask (bit n is layer n). -1 (default) looks at all layers.
@param mask_high The layers 32 to 63, as bits 0 to 31 of a mask. -1 (default) looks at all layers.
@param sensors 1 also finds sensors (see `PhysicsSensor`); 0 (default) leaves them out.
@param world The physics world, 0 (default) for the default world.
@returns The entity of the body that was hit, or 0 if there is none.
@gap The original has no such command. This is an extension; programs that use it do not compile with the original Blitz3D.
